title: Iran to Declare New 'Restricted Zone' Outside Strait of Hormuz, Sanctioning Non-Coordinating Ships
detail: Mohsen Rezaei, Secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, said Iran would announce a new 'restricted zone' outside the Strait of Hormuz 'in the coming days,' extending from the line where the US naval blockade begins, through the strait, and into the Persian Gulf. Ships transiting the zone without coordinating with Iran would be placed on Tehran's sanctions list, affecting their insurance coverage and future passage rights. Rezaei framed the move as part of a broader strategic shift to increase pressure on Washington, and separately said maps for a new international shipping corridor through Iranian and Omani waters had been agreed and were expected to be signed soon. The announcement came two days after the US struck three Iranian oil tankers near Kharg Island and the Gulf of Oman; tanker traffic through Hormuz fell to a four-month low.

title: Iranian Rial Hits New Low (~228,000 Tomans/$1) as Domestic Gasoline Shortage Deepens
detail: Iran's currency crisis deepened further, with the US dollar reaching approximately 228,000 tomans (2.28M rial) on the open market — a new record low — driving inflation that is 'directly affecting household purchasing power, production, and employment' per Iranian economic reporting. Domestic gasoline consumption now exceeds 148 million liters/day of production capacity, with the naval blockade complicating fuel-import workarounds. Housing costs have doubled in some Tehran neighborhoods, forcing families to cut back on nutrition and education spending. Iran's Economy Minister Ali Madanizadeh said reform responsibility lies with Tehran, 'not with the US Treasury,' as Washington's sanctions campaign continues.
